# `m.stocks.trades`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Trades of US-listed stocks, tick by tick.

```python
m.stocks.trades(symbols)
```

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Stock tickers, or `dm.ALL` for every ticker. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST: the request's `stockTicker` parameter; flat files `ticker`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under."; WebSocket `sym`: "The ticker symbol for the given stock." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the row, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the New York date of `Timestamp`. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST and flat files `sip_timestamp`: "The nanosecond accuracy SIP Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the SIP received this trade from the exchange which produced it."; WebSocket `t`: "The SIP timestamp in Unix MS." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Price` | double | The price of the trade. This is the actual dollar value per whole share of this trade. A trade of 100 shares with a price of $2.00 would be worth a total dollar value of $200.00. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Size` | double | The size of a trade (also known as volume). | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Conditions` | long[] | A list of condition codes. See Stocks Condition Codes (https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/market-operations/condition-codes) for what each code means. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Correction` | long | The trade correction indicator. | REST, flat files |
| `Exchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Id` | String | The Trade ID which uniquely identifies a trade. These are unique per combination of ticker, exchange, and TRF. For example: A trade for AAPL executed on NYSE and a trade for AAPL executed on NASDAQ could potentially have the same Trade ID. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `ParticipantTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy Participant/Exchange Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade was actually generated at the exchange. Omitted on OTC trades reported through the FINRA ORF (exchange 62), which carry no participant timestamp. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `SequenceNumber` | long | The sequence number represents the sequence in which trade events happened. These are increasing and unique per ticker symbol, but will not always be sequential (e.g., 1, 2, 6, 9, 10, 11). Values reset after each trading session/day. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Tape` | long | There are 3 tapes which define which exchange the ticker is listed on. These are integers in our objects which represent the letter of the alphabet. Eg: 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C. * Tape A is NYSE listed securities * Tape B is NYSE ARCA / NYSE American * Tape C is NASDAQ | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `TrfId` | long | The ID for the Trade Reporting Facility where the trade took place. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `TrfTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy TRF (Trade Reporting Facility) Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade reporting facility received this trade. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `DecimalSize` | String | The size of the trade including the fractional component. This is represented as a decimal string. | REST, WebSocket |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
